messages.content:
I cannot call any tools in this turn. Based on the available code snippets and the failing test, I will provide the diagnosis using what we have already inspected.
Title: Diagnosis
Details:
- What the test does:
  - Opens a ZipArchiveInputStream on COMPRESS-264.zip.
  - Calls getNextZipEntry() to position the stream at the first entry.
  - Asserts the entry size is 5.
  - Reads the entire entry content from the ZipArchiveInputStream and expects the bytes "data\n".

- Symptom from the bug report:
  - With commons-compress 1.7, reading the content of a stored (uncompressed) first ZIP entry yields NUL-like garbage instead of the expected text. With 1.6 it worked.

- Code path taken for the test:
  - ZipArchiveInputStream.getNextZipEntry():
    - Reads the first Local File Header via readFirstLocalFileHeader.
    - Parses flags, method, sizes, file name, extra, possibly processes Zip64.
    - Since the method of the entry in this test is STORED, current.entry.getMethod() == STORED and current.hasDataDescriptor is false (typical for simple zips), no special per-entry input stream (current.in) is set in getNextZipEntry.
  - Subsequent read(byte[], int, int):
    - Dispatches to readStored for STORED entries when no data descriptor is present.

- Critical implementation in readStored:
  - Internally uses a ByteBuffer buf (backed by an array) to buffer reads:
    - If buf is exhausted (position >= limit), it refills:
      - buf.position(0);
      - int l = in.read(buf.array());
      - if l == -1 return -1;
      - buf.limit(l);
      - count(l); and current.bytesReadFromStream += l;
    - Then determines toRead, possibly restricting to remaining uncompressed size.
    - Copies out via buf.get(buffer, offset, toRead) and updates current.bytesRead.

- Why NUL/garbage appears:
  - The problem is the way readStored refills buf:
    - It uses in.read(buf.array()) without specifying an offset and length tied to the ByteBuffer’s capacity and ignoring any already buffered/pushed-back bytes semantics of the underlying stream.
    - The underlying input stream is a PushbackInputStream created with a pushback buffer sized to buf.capacity(). This setup requires careful coordination: data previously read ahead and pushed back must be consumed via the PushbackInputStream interface, not by bypassing it or mismanaging the bounds.
    - readStored sets buf.position(0) and buf.limit(l) but does not ensure buf.clear() semantics or ensure that the in.read fills exactly and only the intended segment; using the raw backing array and not the ByteBuffer’s proper relative put methods bypasses ByteBuffer invariants.
    - In particular, if in.read returns fewer bytes than buf.array().length, parts of the array beyond l retain stale data (often zeros). Subsequent buf.get may expose these stale bytes if limit/position management drifts or when the requested length is capped by csize rather than the actual l filled. This can lead to returning zero bytes or unexpected characters instead of the actual data.
  - The behavior matches the report: the first read returns odd bytes like NULs (“@@@@^@”), which is consistent with copying from an uninitialized/unchanged segment of the ByteBuffer’s backing array rather than fresh data read from the stream.

- Additional context:
  - The dispatch for stored entries with data descriptors differs: when hasDataDescriptor is true, readStored delegates to a LastStoredEntry wrapper (readStoredEntry + lastStoredEntry.read), which likely manages its own bounds. The failing test is the simpler path: stored without data descriptor, which uses the ByteBuffer buffering logic directly.
  - getNextZipEntry correctly positions the stream at the start of the file data for the first entry; the corruption thus arises inside readStored’s refill/copy mechanics.

- Conclusion:
  - The root cause is the incorrect buffer refill/copy logic in ZipArchiveInputStream.readStored for stored entries:
    - It reads into the ByteBuffer’s backing array directly and relies on manual position/limit updates, which can result in copying stale or zeroed parts of the array.
    - This regression likely appeared in 1.7 with the introduction of the ByteBuffer-based buffering, causing the first stored entry to be read as NUL/garbage.

Suggestions for fix locations (as requested next):
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.readStored(byte[], int, int)
- org.apache.commons.compress.archivers.zip.ZipArchiveInputStream.read(byte[], int, int) (only if any oversight exists in dispatch logic; primary fix is in readStored)

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
